_README: Documented reference thresholds for the general adult population (see url). They are NOT spaceflight-specific flight rules, which are not public. Two kinds of bounds: 'attention_low/high' (documented, out of the normal range but not an emergency) raise the level to Watch; 'critical_low/high' (documented emergency or clinically significant level) are the ONLY rules that can trigger Critical. null or missing = no documented bound, so only the personal-baseline rules apply. A bound is strict (value must be beyond it) unless '<bound>_inclusive' is true. 'source_low'/'source_high' override 'source' for one side. '<bound>_reason' is the reason shown to the astronaut ({value} and {unit} are filled in); the source is appended in parentheses.

heart_rate.attention_high_reason: Above the normal resting range of {value} {unit}
heart_rate.note: AHA: normal resting heart rate is 60-100 bpm; above 100 at rest is tachycardia. That is outside the normal range, not by itself an emergency, so it is attention (Watch), not critical. No low bound: below 60 (bradycardia) is common in fit people, so it is left to the personal baseline.

bp_systolic.attention_low_reason: Below {value} {unit}, defined as low blood pressure
bp_systolic.note: AHA: higher than 180 systolic = hypertensive crisis, consult a doctor immediately -> critical. NHLBI: low blood pressure is lower than 90/60 mm Hg, but it is often harmless without symptoms -> attention (Watch), not critical.

bp_diastolic.attention_low_reason: Below {value} {unit}, defined as low blood pressure
bp_diastolic.note: AHA: higher than 120 diastolic = hypertensive crisis -> critical. NHLBI: low blood pressure is lower than 90/60 mm Hg, often harmless without symptoms -> attention (Watch), not critical.

glucose.attention_high_reason: Above {value} {unit}, the level at which ADA guidance says to check for ketones
glucose.note: ADA/EASD: below 54 mg/dL = clinically significant (level 2) hypoglycemia -> critical. ADA: above 240 mg/dL, check for ketones: a reason to check and follow up, not by itself an emergency -> attention (Watch). Both come from diabetes care guidance.

temperature.note: CDC: fever = measured temperature of at least 38 °C (100.4 °F); on a long mission, far from care, a fever is treated as critical. CDC: below 35 °C (95 °F) is an emergency (hypothermia) -> critical.

sleep_hours.note: Adults should sleep at least 7 hours per night (AASM, CDC). This is a health recommendation, not an escalation threshold, so it is used in guidance only.

mood.note: Self-reported 1-5 scale, not a clinical instrument: no escalation threshold.
